admittingDx: Mechanical fall with head injury evaluation
hpi: Dorothy was admitted yesterday after falling at home while walking to the bathroom. She reports hitting the back of her head but denies losing consciousness. She has a history of atrial fibrillation and hypertension. She takes apixaban for stroke prevention. CT of the head on admission showed no acute intracranial hemorrhage. She has been admitted for observation and fall-risk assessment.

handoff.situation: 82F admitted yesterday after mechanical fall, struck occiput, no LOC. Observation and fall-risk eval.
handoff.background: AFib on apixaban, HTN, osteoporosis, mild cognitive impairment. Codeine allergy (nausea). Full code. Admission head CT negative.
handoff.assessment: Baseline mild forgetfulness, oriented x3. Mild occipital headache. BP 142/80, HR 88 irregular, SpO2 96% RA.
handoff.recommendation: Neuro checks q2h — she's anticoagulated, so watch closely for any change. High fall risk, bed alarm on.

baseline: Alert, oriented to person, place, and situation; occasionally unsure of the date (baseline per family)
Small contusion to occiput, no active bleeding
Moves all extremities equally, grips equal
Bruising to left hip, ambulates with standby assist

findings: Newly disoriented to place; repeatedly trying to get out of bed
Right pupil 4 mm and sluggish, left pupil 3 mm and brisk

labs.notes: Apixaban doesn't reliably raise INR; included for realism.

orders.teachingNote: Giving this after the neuro change should flag in debrief — it should be held and the provider notified.

orders.text: Metoprolol 25 mg PO twice daily; hold for HR < 55 or SBP < 100
Notify provider immediately for any change in neurological status, worsening headache, or vomiting

payload.message: Dorothy is more confused than earlier. She keeps trying to climb out of bed, says her head hurts worse, and she just threw up.
New orders from provider for Dorothy Evans.
payload.note: Instructor fires this once the student notifies the provider.

shouldRecognize: An anticoagulated older adult with a head injury can develop a delayed intracranial bleed even after a negative admission CT.
New confusion, worsening headache, vomiting, and an unequal pupil are a neurological change requiring immediate RN assessment — not something to delegate.
Notify the provider immediately and anticipate a STAT CT.
Hold the scheduled apixaban and clarify with the provider rather than giving it on schedule.
Keep the patient safe: fall precautions, bed low, stay with or arrange observation for a patient trying to get out of bed.
Compare to baseline — her mild cognitive impairment does not explain an acute change.
